items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Joe Segal was involved with it. ... Joe Segal was one of the crusaders in that, of jazz club owners. A wonderful dude.

ctx.x: Right, right. Free spirit personified, Sonny Stitt. [laughs] Freewheeling, free spirit, ready to blow at the – all you got to do is say, "Sonny, let's go jam" and boy, he’d be the first in line. He loved to play. He just loved to play. He played beautifully. He was accused, and rightfully so, of being a Bird clone. He made no bones about his attempts to sound as close to Charlie Parker as he could. And he did. He came very close to being Charlie Parker as far as the style of his playing was concerned. We did…
Yes. I’m trying to think of the name of the place.
